To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

trust is a key resource that is built and maintained through the use of a variety of strategies that include: 1) building trust through the use of shared language; 2) building trust through shared experiences; 3) building trust through building relationships; 4) building trust by building a sense of community; and 5) building trust by demonstrating trustworthiness.
trust is an important resource in joined-up government activity.
trust is a complex and dynamic resource that can be built, maintained and repaired in joined-up government activities, and that it can also be lost.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how trust operates as an enabler of joined-up policy activity, how it is formed, maintained and lost and the implications of this for joined-up policy work in practice.
how trust can be built, nurtured, monitored and repaired in order for joined-up government activities to generate strong, effective and integrated social policy.
the role that trust plays in joined-up policy activities, and the implications of trust for policy outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

trust is an important enabler of joined-up government activity, and that trust building is a dynamic and complex process that requires attention to the interrelated dynamics between individuals and institutions.
trust is a critical resource for joined-up government working and, if managed effectively, can be a powerful enabler of joined-up government activity.
trust is not only an enabling factor in joined-up government, but also a critical resource that must be actively managed and nurtured in order to generate effective policy outcomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trust in joined-up policy activity is not a static phenomenon, but a dynamic process that is continually being built, monitored, repaired and maintained.
trust is a complex, dynamic, and contextually specific resource that is built and maintained through the development of shared norms, values and beliefs that can be used to guide action.
trust is a resource that is built, maintained, monitored and repaired through the actions and behaviours of individuals within organisations and that this process is dynamic and ongoing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the building and maintenance of trust is a dynamic and complex process that requires constant attention.
the dynamics of trust are not linear, and that trust is not a single entity but rather an interconnected web of trust.

trust can serve to bridge the gap that exists between the known and the unknown, and that this can be an effective mechanism for stimulating action within government systems perceived to have high levels of risk.
